For each measurement, NightBaseline takes your last 14 to 28 nights and finds the middle value. Your usual range is that middle value plus or minus how much your nights normally vary. Unusual single nights barely move it.
It needs 7 nights to start. Nights shorter than 3 hours and nights without readings are left out.
A night counts as outside when it is clearly away from your middle value, both compared with your normal variation and by a minimum amount, so tiny changes don\'t count.

It means a measurement was different from your own recent nights. It isn\'t a diagnosis. One measurement often moves on its own; when two or more move on the same night, NightBaseline sends a note. Late meals, alcohol, travel, hard training, a cold, new medication or how the device sits can all play a part.
If you feel unwell or are worried, talk to a health professional.

NightBaseline is not a medical device. It doesn\'t diagnose, treat or prevent any condition and can\'t tell you whether you are ill. It only compares your night measurements with your own recent nights.
